subject.title: fix(browser): bound client fetch success JSON reads

question: Should browser-control HTTP success responses be capped at 16 MiB, accepting that oversized external browser-control responses now fail instead of resolving?
rationale: The patch is the right owner-boundary fix for the buffering bug, but it intentionally fail-closes an existing success path for any external service returning more than 16 MiB of JSON.

options.title: Accept the 16 MiB cap
options.body: Merge this PR with the new size-boundary contract because it matches existing provider JSON caps and prevents unbounded buffering.

options.title: Choose a different contract
options.body: Ask for a different browser-specific limit or a named shared browser JSON helper before merge if 16 MiB is not the desired product boundary.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Keep the PR open until maintainers confirm whether any supported browser-control response can legitimately exceed the proposed cap.

recommendation.title: Accept the 16 MiB cap
recommendation.body: Merge this PR with the new size-boundary contract because it matches existing provider JSON caps and prevents unbounded buffering.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the current-main browser client fetch implementation in the local blame/history evidence.
